judged_text: APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED is a raw string concatenation of two env values (`process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`), so the constant is the value of the secret rather than a boolean, and is enabled solely by setting two env vars with no feature flag. Operators who set CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET for any other purpose (it is a generically-named webhook secret) silently activate credential sync, redirecting all OAuth refreshes to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT when set — behavior cannot be toggled independently of the secret and leaks the secret's value into any place the 'boolean' is serialized.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which in JS/TS evaluates to the *second env var’s string value* (or `undefined`), not a boolean. The diff shows this value being used as a flag (`if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT ...)`). That works via truthiness, but it’s easy to misuse later (e.g., serialize/log the exported constant and inadvertently expose the encryption key). The claim that this “redirects all OAuth refreshes” is slightly overstated because `refreshOAuthTokens` also requires `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` and `userId`, but the core issue (non-boolean flag derived from secrets; enablement coupled to env presence) is grounded in the diff.
